items.sentence1: The bank will lend you the money, but only if you can provide a guarantor.
items.before: The bank will lend you the money
fullAnswers: on condition that you can provide
on condition that you can find
on the condition that you provide
on the condition that you find

explanation.en: Part 1: 'but only if' becomes the fixed conditional linker 'on (the) condition that'. Part 2: it is followed by a full clause with its own subject and verb, 'you (can) provide' or 'you (can) find'. 'On the condition that you can provide' would be 7 words, which is too many.
explanation.cs: Část 1: 'but only if' nahradíme spojkou on (the) condition that = pod podmínkou, že. Část 2: následuje celá věta s podmětem a slovesem: you (can) provide / you (can) find. Varianta 'on the condition that you can provide' má 7 slov, to je moc.

items.sentence1: 'Do not open attachments from unknown senders,' the IT manager told the staff.
fullAnswers: warned the staff not to open

explanation.en: Part 1: 'warn' takes a direct object, so the listener follows it: 'warned the staff'. Part 2: a negative command is reported with 'not to' + infinitive ('not to open') or with 'against' + -ing ('against opening'). 'Warned the staff to not open' puts 'not' in the wrong place.
explanation.cs: Část 1: warn má přímý předmět, proto hned za ním stojí the staff. Část 2: zápor rozkazu převedeme jako not to + infinitiv (not to open) nebo against + -ing (against opening). Pořadí 'to not open' je chybné.

items.sentence1: The university is going to publish the exam results next Friday.

explanation.en: Part 1: a planned future event is expressed with 'be due', and the plural subject needs 'are'. Part 2: the results do not publish themselves, so a passive infinitive is needed: 'to be published' (or released / announced). 'Are due out' and 'are due to come out' are also natural and accepted.
explanation.cs: Část 1: plánovanou budoucnost vyjádříme be due (má proběhnout), u množného čísla are due. Část 2: výsledky nikdo 'nepublikuje sám', proto pasivní infinitiv: to be published (released, announced). Uznává se i are due out / are due to come out.

items.sentence1: Sophie postponed telling her boss about the mistake for as long as she could.
items.after: her boss about the mistake for as long as she could.

explanation.en: Part 1: 'postponed' becomes the phrasal verb 'put off' (past tense 'put'); 'held off' is also accepted. Part 2: 'put off' is followed by the -ing form, 'telling', not 'to tell'.
explanation.cs: Část 1: postponed = frázové sloveso put off (minulý čas put, beze změny tvaru); uznává se i held off. Část 2: po put off následuje -ing: telling, nikoli to tell.

items.sentence1: The new manager has greatly influenced the way the office works.

explanation.en: Part 1: the verb 'influenced' becomes the noun phrase 'had a great influence', and the adverb 'greatly' becomes an adjective. Part 2: the noun 'influence' takes the preposition 'on'. 'A great deal of influence on' would be 7 words.
explanation.cs: Část 1: sloveso influenced převedeme na podstatné jméno: has had a great influence; příslovce greatly se mění na přídavné jméno great (huge, major…). Část 2: influence se pojí s předložkou on. 'A great deal of influence on' má 7 slov.

items.sentence1: Working night shifts no longer feels strange to me.

explanation.en: Part 1: 'no longer feels strange' describes a change, so the answer is 'got used to' (or 'become / grown used to'), not 'used to', which is about past habits. Part 2: 'to' here is a preposition, so it is followed by the -ing form: 'working', not 'work'.
explanation.cs: Část 1: jde o změnu (už mi to nepřijde divné), proto get / become used to = zvyknout si. Pozor: samotné used to + infinitiv znamená 'dříve jsem…'. Část 2: to je zde předložka, proto následuje -ing: working, ne work.
